subject.title: fix(memory-host-sdk): do not wipe archive on user-typed [cron: prefix

question: Should OpenClaw continue supporting metadata-free cron archive opacity after removing the user-spoofable `[cron:]` text classifier?
rationale: Same-root sibling reviews treated metadata-free cron archive opacity as security-sensitive, but this PR now carries maintainer-authored commits that choose structured provenance only; automation cannot infer that security-boundary choice.

options.title: Trust structured provenance
options.body: Land this PR once maintainers accept that cron archives without session-store or `sessionKey` metadata are not a supported security boundary.

options.title: Preserve legacy opacity
options.body: Require a non-user-spoofable doctor, migration, or marker-based path for metadata-free cron archives before merging.

options.title: Pause for archive policy
options.body: Hold the PR while maintainers define the permanent reset/deleted cron archive classification contract.

recommendation.title: Trust structured provenance
recommendation.body: Land this PR once maintainers accept that cron archives without session-store or `sessionKey` metadata are not a supported security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned and authored the current follow-up commits refining this exact behavior.
